questions.question:
Study the following information carefully and answer the questions accordingly.

 

Seven people A, B, C, D, E, F and G live in a seven storey building, but not necessarily in the same order. The lowermost floor is numbered 1 and topmost floor is numbered 7. F lives on the middle floor of the building. There is only one floor between F and G. B lives on an even numbered floor. There is only a two floor gap between B and D. A lives above E but below C. E does not live near to B.

 

E lives on which of the following floors?
questions.explanation:
F lives on the middle floor of the building.

There is only one floor between F and G.

B lives on an even numbered floor.

There is only a two floor gap between B and D.

A lives above E but below C.

E does not live near to B.
Case 1: is eliminated.

Hence, the correct ans is "1 floor".

questions.question:
Study the following information carefully and answer the questions accordingly.


Seven people A, B, C, L, M, N and O live on seven different floors in a building but not necessarily in the same order. The ground floor is numbered one and the top floor is numbered seven. L lives on the prime number floor. C lives four floors above L. There are two floors between C and O. There is only one floor between O and A who does not live near to C. N lives above O and lives on an even number floor. B lives above N’s floor and does not live just above N’s floor.


How many floors are there between C and B?
questions.explanation:
L lives on the prime number floor.
C lives four floors above L.

There are two floors between C and O.

There is only one floor between O and A, who does not lives near to C.

N lives above O, and lives on an even number floor.

B lives above N’s floor and does not live just above N’s floor.

Case 2: is eliminated.

Hence, the correct ans is "None".

What is the direction of point R with respect to point Q?

questions.question:
Study the following information carefully and answer the questions accordingly.

 

Eight persons ( A, B, E, Q, R, S, T and V) went to a Zoo in four different months viz. April, May, June and July on two different dates i.e. 11th and 24th.
B went to the zoo in the month having 30 days before A. Two persons went to the zoo between E and T. The person whose name starts with a vowel, didn’t go to the zoo in the month having 30 days. Two persons went to the zoo between R and V. R went to the zoo immediately after E. Two persons went to the zoo between S and B. Q went to the zoo in the same month as S. T went to the zoo on 24th of one of the months. V doesn't go to the zoo in April.

 

Who went to the zoo on the 24th of April?
questions.explanation:
1. Two persons went to the zoo between E and T.

  2. T went to the zoo on 24th of one of the months.

  3. The person whose name starts with a vowel, didn’t go to the zoo in the month having 30 days.

CASE 1

CASE 2

  1. Two persons went to the zoo between R and V.

  2. R went to the zoo immediately after E.

  3. V doesn't go to the zoo in April.

CASE 1

CASE 2

  1. Two persons went to the zoo between S and B.

  2. Q went to the zoo in the same month as S. Therefore, Case 2 is no longer valid.

CASE 1

questions.question:
In each question below some statements are given followed by some conclusions. You have to take the given statements to be true even if they seem to be at variance with commonly known facts. Read all the statements and then decide which of the given conclusions logically follows from the given statements, disregarding commonly known facts.

 

 

Statements:

All girls are social workers.

All social workers are women.

All women are teachers.

Conclusions:

I. All teachers are women.

II. All women are social workers.

III. All social workers are girls.

IV. All girls are teachers.
questions.explanation:
1 does not follow from the last statement, on conversion.

2 does not follow from the second statement, on conversion.

3 does not follow from the first statement, on conversion.

1st and 2nd and 3rd statements give conclusion 4.

questions.question:
In each question below are given two statements followed by two conclusions numbered I and II. You have to take the two given statements to be true even if they seem to be at variance with commonly known facts. Read both the statements and then decide which of the given conclusions logically follows from the given statements, disregarding commonly known facts.

 

Statements:

Some Knife are Hammer.
No Hammer is Blade.

Conclusions:

I. Some Knife are not Blade.
II. Some Blade are not Hammer.
options: Either conclusion I or conclusion II follows
Neither conclusion I nor conclusion II follows
Both conclusion I and conclusion II follow
questions.explanation:
Conclusion 1: It is follow. Some part of Knife is touches Hammer and No Hammer is Blade given so Some Knife are not Blade is definite follow.

Conclusion 2: It is follow. No Hammer is Blade is given so Some Blade are not Hammer is definite follow.

questions.question:
In the question below some statements are given followed by three conclusions I, II and III. You have to take the given statements to be true even if they seem to be at variance with commonly known facts. Read all the conclusions and then decide which of the given conclusions definitely follows from the given statements, disregarding commonly known facts.

 

 

Statements:

All Food are Cereal      

A few Cereal are Grains

Only Cereal are Wheat

Conclusions:

I. At least some Food are Wheat

II. All grains are not Wheat

III. All Food are Wheat
questions.explanation:
Following figure can be formed-

Conclusions:

I. At least some Food are Wheat (False), (There are definite relationship between Wheat and Cereal so any positive relationship with Wheat with others will be false)

II. All grains are not Wheat (True), (There are definite relationship between Wheat and Cereal so any negative relationship with Wheat with others will be true)

III. All Food are Wheat (False), (There are definite relationship between Wheat and Cereal so any positive relationship with Wheat with others will be false)

From the figure, only conclusion II follows.

The 2nd, 3rd, 4th and 8th letters of the word ‘SCRABBLE’ :- C, R, A, E

questions.question: How many numbers between 90 and 750 could be divisible by 8?
questions.explanation:
Given: The numbers exist between 90 and 750 that are divisible by 8.

According to the arithmetic progression (A.P.) formula:

\(a_{\text{n }} = \ a + (n - 1)d\) .

Here, \(a\) and \(a_{n}\) are the first and \(n^{\text{th}}\) term in the sequence, and \(d\) is the common difference between terms.

Calculation:

The numbers are between 90 and 750, divisible by 8:

96, 104, 112, 120,.........., 744.

Where \(a = 96\) , \(d = 8\) and \(a_{n} = 744\)

\(= > \ 96 + (n - 1)\ 8 = 744\)

\(= > \ 8n - 8 = 744 - 96\)

\(= > 8n = 656\)

\(= > n = \frac{656}{8}\)

\(= > n = 82\)

Therefore, there are 82 numbers between 90 and 750 that can be divided by 8.

questions.question: Sita and Gita can do a work in 30 days and 50 days respectively. Sita started the work and left after 3 days. Gita took over and completed the work. In how many days was the total work completed?
questions.explanation:
LCM(30,50) = 150 ( Total work )

Sita’s one day’s work= 5

Sita’s 3 day’s work = 15

Work left= 150 - 15 = 135

Gita's one day’s work= 3

Gita's can do work in = 1353=45 days

So total days = 45+3 = 48 days

Alternate Method:

Sita can do the work in 30 days → 1 day work = 1/30
Gita can do the work in 50 days → 1 day work = 1/50
Sita works for 3 days, then Gita completes the remaining work
We need: Total days to complete the work
Work done by Sita in 3 days
Sita’s 1 day work = 1/30
Work done in 3 days = 3 × 1/30 = 3/30 = 1/10
Remaining work
Remaining work = 1 - 1/10 = 9/10
Time for Gita to finish remaining work
Gita’s 1 day work = 1/50
Time = Remaining work ÷ Gita’s 1 day work
Time = (9/10) ÷ (1/50) = (9/10) × 50 = 45 days
Total time
Total time = Sita’s 3 days + Gita’s 45 days = 48 days
Answer:
Total work was completed in 48 days
